Mr. Hack. Thank you, Mr. Chair. This report outlines various options for committee's consideration regarding the previously approved business development incentive for Maven Water and Environmental Limited who has recently been acquired by integrated sustainability.

As outlined in the report and previously reported to the Standing Policy Committee on Finance, Maven had received the first three years of the business development incentive despite not achieving the FTE requirements in any of those years.

The incentive was provided in these three years based on the flexibility provided for in the policy as Maven continued to actively recruit and the reductions did not appear to be permanent in nature as outlined in the suite of audits.
In the past year integrated sustainability has acquired Maven and requested continuation of the business development incentive.
While the policy does not allow for the transfer of a business development incentive, the history of Maven not achieving the FTE requirements adds complexity to this decision.
The report outlines several options for the consideration of committee.
The administration is recommending option for which would allow for the assignment of the current incentive agreement to integrated sustainability.
However, the city would withhold the economic incentive in the final two years unless the FTE requirement is met.
In addition, this option would not pursue recovery of previously provided incentives to Maven.

This option is recommended as it most closely aligns with the administration's view on the intent of the policy, which allows for flexibility in the event that the FTE shortages are not planned or permanent.
And further supports integrated sustainability, who has outlined a further intent to generate and grow their business within Saskatchewan.
Without there is one recommendation in front of committee and administration be happy to answer any questions there may be.
